title: These men soften their phrases, but such harsh speech needlessly troubles the people; it is neither Scripture's nor the Fathers'
source_text: XLIV. Scio magnos illos viros qui locutionibus ejusmodi utuntur, consequentias istas non admittere, & dicta sua quantum possunt reducere ad sensum bonum atque commodum: sed quantumvis ejusmodi durae locutiones interpretatione benigna emolliantur, Christianae plebis aures non possunt non offendere, & animis audientium non injicere varios scrupulos, absque ulla necessitate. Quid enim opus mordicus adhaerere istis loquendi modis, qui nec diserte sunt in scriptura expressi, nec sunt in usu veterum Ecclesiae Doctorum?
pass_a_gloss: XLIV. I know those great men who use expressions of this kind do not admit these consequences, and reduce their sayings as much as they can to a good and fitting sense: but however much harsh expressions of this kind be softened by kind interpretation, they cannot but offend the ears of the Christian people, and cast various scruples into the minds of hearers, without any necessity. For what need is there to cling with the teeth to these modes of speaking, which are neither expressly stated in scripture, nor are in use among the ancient Doctors of the Church?
pass_b_english: I know that the great men who use expressions of this kind do not admit these consequences, and bring their statements, as far as they can, to a sound and acceptable sense.

But however much such harsh expressions are softened by charitable interpretation, they cannot fail to offend the ears of Christian people and to plant various doubts in the minds of those who hear them, and that without any need. What need is there to cling tooth and nail to ways of speaking that are neither stated outright in Scripture nor used by the ancient doctors of the Church?

lemmas.latin: Christianae plebis aures non possunt non offendere
lemmas.gloss: cannot but offend the ears of the Christian people
to cling with the teeth to these modes of speaking
